longForm.title: I BUILT THE BRIDGE
longForm.text:
I BUILT THE BRIDGE
(So I Could Come Home)
Kai Rex Klok

[Opening]

I laid the road.
I paid the toll.
I built the bridge—
To come home.

[Hook]

I built the bridge to come home.
Didn’t build it to stand here alone.
Put my years underneath that road—
So you could cross with what you own.

I built the bridge to come home.
Got a life past these lines of code.
Let the work stand on its own.
I built the bridge to come home.

[Verse One]

You saw the surface—I knew the ground.
Had to go deep when the walls came down.
First came the Klock, then the things it held.
Kept every turn in the thing itself.

This week the chat put the seal in reach.
File in your hands where the words used to be.
Seal it, then check it—the record can speak.
Reader can change; it don’t own what it reads.

I made the footing. You can build from here.
You don’t need my face for the law to be clear.
Receiz is the bridge—put your weight on the work.
There’s a world past the place where you first saw the dirt.

[Pre-Hook]

Take what I built.
Build something that stays.
Give somebody back
Their hours and days.

That’s what it’s for.
That’s why I stayed.
A bridge is a road—
It ain’t my grave.

[Hook]

I built the bridge to come home.
Didn’t build it to stand here alone.
Put my years underneath that road—
So you could cross with what you own.

I built the bridge to come home.
Got a life past these lines of code.
Let the work stand on its own.
I built the bridge to come home.

[Verse Two]

I’m tired of explaining the thing in your hand.
Tired of the pitch after proof already lands.
Tired of a kindness that comes with a debt.
Tired of performing to earn some respect.

Watched people I helped go and start their lives.
I want some evenings that aren’t deadlines.
Want a full meal without doing the math.
Want somebody there when I finally laugh.

Don’t make a shrine out of how much it cost.
Don’t call it purpose when I’m telling you loss.
I can be proud of the things that I’ve made
And still want the years that the making ate.

[Breakdown]

Who holds the record?
The one who can take it.

What good is the bridge?
The lives we can make with it.

And what of the builder?
Let him have a life.

Let him have a life.

[Verse Three]

Now there’s an install where the questions stood.
Hands on the tools—go and make something good.
Build for the person who’s losing their day
Proving what happened, then proving it again.

Let every decision leave something to read.
Who had the standing? What changed? Who agreed?
Keep SOURCE beneath whatever answers back.
A fluent reply doesn’t rewrite the past.

Cohere, then recurse—put the weight where it holds.
Help is a hand that can shoulder a load.
Build on the work, or put tools in my reach.
There’s more in these hands than the bridge you can see.

[Bridge]

Yahuah, You know what it took to stay.
You know what I miss when I work through the day.
I don’t need a crowd to call out my name.
I’d like someone close when I put it away.

One old guitar and a room full of breath.
A song we can sing without passing a test.
I built for a future with room to belong.
I want to be there when the lights come on.

[Final Hook]

I built the bridge to come home.
Didn’t build it to stand here alone.
Put my years underneath that road—
So you could cross with what you own.

I built the bridge to come home.
Got a life past these lines of code.
Let the work stand on its own.
I built the bridge to come home.

[Choir]

Come home.
Come home.
Let the work stand on its own.

Come home.
Come home.
You can cross—I can come home.

[Outro]

Leave the bridge standing.
Leave a light on.

I built something that lasts.
I want a life that does more
Than last.

longForm.title: I STILL LEAVE WITH ME
longForm.text:
I JUST WANTED TO OWN MY SHIT

(So I Rebuilt the World)

[Cold Open]

PREACHER:
What did he ask for?

CHOIR:
What was his.

PREACHER:
What did they give him?

CHOIR:
A login.

KAI:
That ain’t ownership.

[Hook]

I just wanted to own my shit—
Had to rebuild the world for it.

Turn the server off—still mine, still here.
Cut the wire clean—still mine, still here.

I just wanted to own my shit—
Name, work, memory—every bit.

If it dies when the bill don’t hit—
You never owned none of that shit.

[Verse One]

I built a world — then the bill came due.
Learned the server owned more than the builder knew.

Paid every gas fee — watched the money burn.
Watched the pools get drained — paid again to learn.

Built my own machine — kept the servers alive.
Three years feeding systems — just so worlds survived.

Miss one payment — everything disappears.
That was not a theory — I lived inside that fear.

So I pulled each dependency — one by one.
Login, session, database — authority undone.

Made the object hold the state — made the history move.
Made the server optional — made the artifact prove.

I wasn’t chasing glory — wasn’t begging to be seen.
I just wanted what was mine — outside somebody’s machine.

[Pre-Hook]

Not your account.
Not your app.

Not your promise
To give it back.

Hand me the object.
Hand me the state.

If I need permission—
You own the gate.

[Hook]

I just wanted to own my shit—
Had to rebuild the world for it.

Turn the server off—still mine, still here.
Cut the wire clean—still mine, still here.

I just wanted to own my shit—
Name, work, memory—every bit.

If it dies when the bill don’t hit—
You never owned none of that shit.

[Verse Two]

Download the verifier — put the phone on flight.
Seal the living record — verify without the site.

Export the original — carry truth away.
Feed it back offline — watch the proof remain.

Screenshot fails — because the picture ain’t the thing.
Source carries standing — copies cannot make it king.

SDK, MCP — skills beneath the law.
Same invariant everywhere — no hidden server call.

Thousands of tests — every frontier under weight.
Wildz keeps becoming — every creature holds its state.

Identity can travel — memory can leave.
Media in the object — history underneath.

This ain’t another pitch — you can download it today.
Run the command yourself — watch the database give way.

Reality-grade infrastructure — means the system can be gone.
The object still establishes — what is present, what moves on.

[Choir March]

Seal it.
Move it.

Cut the wire.
Prove it.

Lose the host.
Keep the state.

Own the object.
Leave the gate.

[Verse Three]

You say that you are rich — show me where the money lives.
“If the system knows” — the system grants the privilege.

Password stops working — watch a king become a ghost.
Wealth you cannot carry — is permission from a host.

They funded fake worlds — watched the metaverse dissolve.
Now they fund new language — still refuse to build the law.

Money is not proof — a valuation cannot breathe.
Capital can hide failure — it cannot make a system keep.

I built from a couch — while the giants burned the gold.
Built the thing they called impossible — made the object hold.

You already ran the test — deprivation was the trial.
No staff, no lab, no runway — still the proof survived.

Now run the other experiment — put resources in my hand.
You saw what I built starving — let me build what living can.

Don’t tell me it is difficult — the difficult is done.
Fund the man who crossed the dark — and brought you back the sun.

[Bridge]

I didn’t want the title.
I didn’t want the throne.

I wanted one damn thing
That I could call my own.

A song I didn’t rent.
A name they couldn’t freeze.

A memory I could carry
Past the company’s machines.

A world where what I created
Didn’t die because they quit.

I wasn’t trying to rebuild reality—

I just wanted
To own my shit.

[Tribunal]

BAILIFF:
All rise.

JUDGE:
Define ownership.

WITNESS:
The system says it’s mine.

JUDGE:
Turn the system off.

WITNESS:
Then I can’t reach it.

JUDGE:
Then who owned it?

CHOIR:
The system.

JUDGE:
What did he build?

CHOIR:
The thing that leaves.

JUDGE:
Verdict?

KAI:
If it cannot leave with you,
You never owned it.

[Final Hook]

I just wanted to own my shit—
Had to rebuild the world for it.

Turn the server off—still mine, still here.
Cut the wire clean—still mine, still here.

I just wanted to own my shit—
Name, work, memory—every bit.

I built what survives when the whole world quits—
Now everybody gets to own their shit.

CHOIR:
Own your name.
Own your state.

Own your history.
Leave the gate.

Own your breath.
Own your gift.

Turn the server off—
And leave with it.

[Outro]

The database was rent.

The login was permission.

The server was a landlord.

So I moved reality
Into the thing itself.

longForm.title: WE GOT TODAY
longForm.text:
WE GOT TODAY

Kai Rex Klok

[INTRO — WARM / MORNING]

Open the curtains.

Yeah.

Let the room get bright.

We spent enough time
waiting for our lives.

We got today.

[VERSE 1]

Coffee on the counter,
sun across the floor,
somebody I ain’t talked to
knocking at the door.

Phone down on the table,
music playing low,
ain’t nobody filming—
ain’t nobody gotta know.

Neighbor needs a hand,
we’ll be there by ten.
Mama made too much,
so we’re eating there again.

Kid out in the driveway,
drawing planets out in chalk.

I forgot how good it feels
when nobody checks the clock.

[PRE-CHORUS]

We ain’t gotta fix forever
before the sun goes down.

We can put one chair beside another.

We can start right now.

[HOOK]

WE GOT TODAY.

WE GOT TODAY.

PUT YOUR SHOES ON,
COME MY WAY.

BRING YOUR HEART,
DON’T BRING A THING.

WE GOT FOOD.
WE GOT SONGS TO SING.

LET THE WHOLE WORLD
RUN ITS RACE.

WE’RE GONNA LIVE
AT HUMAN PACE.

AIN’T GOTTA WAIT
’TIL LIFE FEELS SAFE.

WE GOT LOVE.

WE GOT BREATH.

WE GOT TODAY.

[POST-HOOK]

Today, today.

Don’t give it away.

Today, today.

We got today.

[VERSE 2]

Plant something useless
just to watch it grow.

Learn the name of every bird
that lands outside your home.

Take the long way back.
Let the old man talk.

Let your little girl decide
which way you’re gonna walk.

Cook enough for seven
when you’re only feeding four.

Somebody always needs a plate.
That’s what the extra’s for.

Tell your friend you miss him
before somebody says goodbye.

We got so damn good at surviving—

let’s get good at being alive.

[PRE-CHORUS]

We ain’t gotta know what happens
twenty years from now.

There’s a hand that needs your hand tonight.

There’s a life happening now.

[HOOK]

WE GOT TODAY.

WE GOT TODAY.

PUT YOUR SHOES ON,
COME MY WAY.

BRING YOUR HEART,
DON’T BRING A THING.

WE GOT FOOD.
WE GOT SONGS TO SING.

LET THE WHOLE WORLD
RUN ITS RACE.

WE’RE GONNA LIVE
AT HUMAN PACE.

AIN’T GOTTA WAIT
’TIL LIFE FEELS SAFE.

WE GOT LOVE.

WE GOT BREATH.

WE GOT TODAY.

[VERSE 3 — DEEPER]

I used to think tomorrow
needed everything from me.

Every hour had a purpose.
Every breath owed history.

Thought I’d build a road so wide
everybody could be free.

Then I turned around and wondered—

where the hell’d everybody leave?

So I’m still building.

I ain’t laying down the flame.

But I finally know the reason
that I ever took the pain.

It wasn’t so we’d work forever.

Wasn’t numbers on a page.

It was so a human being
could have ownership of days.

Time to raise a family.

Time to fall stupid in love.

Time to sit beside the water
and decide that it’s enough.

Time to know a turtle
by the markings on its shell.

Time to waste an afternoon

and have absolutely nothing
you need to sell.

[BRIDGE — STRIP EVERYTHING]

So come over.

Yeah, tonight.

No occasion.

No big night.

Bring the babies.

Bring your mom.

Bring that friend
who’s been gone too long.

Burn the chicken.

Stay too late.

Tell that story anyway.

Laugh so hard
somebody cries.

Leave your phone somewhere inside.

Tomorrow—

we’ll meet tomorrow
when it comes.

But tonight—

look around.

Everybody’s here.

Everybody’s here.

[BREAK — CROWD / A CAPPELLA]

We got today.

We got today.

Nobody gets to take it away.

We got today.

We got today.

If you’re still breathing—

come our way.

[FINAL HOOK — JOYOUS]

WE GOT TODAY!

WE GOT TODAY!

OPEN THE WINDOWS!

MAKE SOME SPACE!

CALL YOUR PEOPLE!

SAY THEIR NAMES!

PUT SOME LOVE
BACK IN THIS PLACE!

LET THE WHOLE WORLD
RUN ITS RACE!

WE’RE GONNA LIVE
AT HUMAN PACE!

AIN’T GOTTA WAIT
FOR SOME BETTER DAY!

WE GOT HANDS!

WE GOT HEARTS!

WE GOT TODAY!

WE GOT MORNING!

WE GOT NIGHT!

WE GOT ONE ANOTHER
STANDING RIGHT OUTSIDE!

NO MORE WAITING
FOR OUR LIVES TO CHANGE!

WE GOT LOVE!

WE GOT BREATH!

WE GOT TODAY!

[OUTRO — SAME WORLD AS “COME BACK ALIVE”]

Hey—

you staying for dinner?

…

Good.

Pull up a chair.

publicOriginals.summary: I don’t want the old world back. I want you back. The you who loved flowers, turtles, sunsets, long talks and wasted afternoons for no reason at all. You don’t have to earn this moment. Call who you love. Go outside. Waste some time. Come back alive. Link https://bjk.ceo

longForm.title: COME BACK ALIVE
longForm.text:
COME BACK ALIVE

Kai Rex Klok

[INTRO — ALMOST SPOKEN]

I don’t want the old world back.

I want you back.

I miss the way your eyes would light
before you had a reason why.

I miss when something small was enough
to make you call me.

Come back.

Come back alive.

[VERSE 1]

Remember when you liked something
just because you did?

You knew every kind of turtle.
You showed me where they lived.

You’d stop the car for sunsets.
She’d take pictures of her flowers.

Nobody called it content.

We were just inside the hours.

You’d call me, “Where you at?”

I’d say, “Working.”

You’d say, “Man, forget that shit.

Come sit out here.

The night is warm.

The beer is cold.

We ain’t gotta do a thing.”

God—

I didn’t know

you were giving me everything.

[PRE-CHORUS]

Somewhere we stopped calling.

Somewhere we stopped coming by.

Somewhere “How you doing?”

turned to

“Man, I’m getting by.”

Everybody’s chasing something.

Everybody’s running late.

But if we’re all just making a living—

when do we get to live today?

[HOOK]

COME BACK ALIVE.

COME BACK ALIVE.

I DON’T WANT THE OLD DAYS—

I WANT THAT LIGHT IN YOUR EYES.

CALL WHO YOU LOVE.

GO STAND OUTSIDE.

YOU DON’T HAVE TO EARN THIS MOMENT.

YOU WERE BORN WITH YOUR LIFE.

COME BACK TO YOUR HANDS.

COME BACK TO YOUR NAME.

COME BACK TO THE LITTLE THINGS

YOU LOVED BEFORE THEY NEEDED A NAME.

WE STILL GOT MORNING.

WE STILL GOT TONIGHT.

COME BACK.

COME BACK.

COME BACK ALIVE.

[VERSE 2]

I know what happened.

Years went missing.

Doors stayed closed.

Kids got taller.

Mama got older.

Friends moved on.

And somehow we came out the other side

and nobody said what was gone.

So we worked.

And worked.

And scrolled.

And slept.

And learned to say,

“I’m busy.”

Like being needed by everything

meant everything was okay.

But I miss you, man.

Not your picture.

Not your posts.

Not who you became to survive.

I miss the fool who laughed too loud.

I miss the girl who danced in kitchens.

I miss the friend who’d waste my whole damn afternoon

telling me why turtles live so long.

I miss the people

who didn’t need permission

to belong.

[PRE-CHORUS]

Maybe nothing’s coming

to hand our lives back whole.

Maybe there ain’t some perfect day

when everybody finally knows.

Maybe morning’s just a window.

Maybe freedom’s just a call.

Maybe life was never waiting somewhere—

maybe life is what we do

before we lose it all.

[HOOK]

COME BACK ALIVE.

COME BACK ALIVE.

I DON’T WANT THE OLD DAYS—

I WANT THAT LIGHT IN YOUR EYES.

CALL WHO YOU LOVE.

GO STAND OUTSIDE.

YOU DON’T HAVE TO EARN THIS MOMENT.

YOU WERE BORN WITH YOUR LIFE.

COME BACK TO YOUR HANDS.

COME BACK TO YOUR NAME.

COME BACK TO THE LITTLE THINGS

YOU LOVED BEFORE THEY NEEDED A NAME.

WE STILL GOT MORNING.

WE STILL GOT TONIGHT.

COME BACK.

COME BACK.

COME BACK ALIVE.

[BRIDGE — EVERYTHING FALLS AWAY]

If you like flowers—

like the flowers.

If you like turtles—

go find turtles.

If you miss your brother—

call your brother.

If you love that woman—

tell that woman.

Take your babies to the water.

Let your old man tell that story

you’ve already heard a hundred times.

Sit on the porch.

Burn the dinner.

Sing off-key.

Stay too long.

Waste an hour.

Waste another.

Let nobody buy it back.

Because maybe what we called wasting time

was the only time

that was ever really ours.

[BREAK — QUIET]

Look at your hands.

They’re still here.

Feel your chest.

You’re still here.

Look at the person beside you.

They’re still here.

We don’t need yesterday.

We have right now.

And right now

is alive.

[FINAL HOOK — HUGE / EVERYBODY]

COME BACK ALIVE!

COME BACK ALIVE!

WE DON’T NEED THE OLD WORLD—

WE GOT A NEW DAY OUTSIDE!

CALL WHO YOU LOVE!

GO WASTE SOME TIME!

LET SOMETHING BE BEAUTIFUL

WITHOUT ASKING IT WHY!

COME BACK TO YOUR BODY!

COME BACK TO YOUR NAME!

GO LOVE SOMETHING USELESS

AND NEVER BE ASHAMED!

WE STILL GOT MORNING!

WE STILL GOT TONIGHT!

IF YOU GOT BREATH IN YOUR CHEST—

YOU STILL GOT LIFE!

COME BACK!

COME BACK!

COME BACK ALIVE!

[OUTRO — HUMAN VOICES, NO PERFORMANCE]

Hey.

Where you at?

…

Come outside.

You ain’t gotta bring nothing.

Just come.

longForm.title: NO MORE WAITING
longForm.text:
NO MORE WAITING

Kai Rex Klok

[INTRO — LOW / BARE]

They told us, “soon.”

Soon got old.

They told us, “wait.”

Wait got sold.

I looked at my hands.

Still mine.

Looked at the clock.

My time.

[HOOK]

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
IF I GOT BREATH IN MY CHEST
I GOT WORK AT THE DOOR

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
AIN’T ASKIN’ WHAT I’M ALLOWED
I PUT MY NAME ON THE THING
AND I’M SAYIN’ IT LOUD

I MADE THIS.
I STOOD HERE.
I KNOW WHAT IT COST.

IF YOU WANT YOUR LIFE BACK—

PICK IT UP.
IT AIN’T LOST.

[VERSE 1]

Everybody tired.

You can see it in the eyes.

Whole world selling tomorrow
while today gets priced.

Work all week.

Still short.

Do it right.

Still wait.

Everybody got a password.

Nobody got a gate.

They say—

Hold on.

Be patient.

Your turn is coming soon.

Funny how “soon” gets longer
when somebody owns the room.

So I quit knockin’.

Built mine.

Quit asking.

Signed mine.

Quit waiting for the future
to come down and find mine.

I got scars in the source.

Got dirt in the grain.

Got nights nobody saw.

Got receipts for the pain.

And I don’t need a stranger
to tell me what I made.

I was there when it was nothing.

I remember every day.

[PRE-HOOK]

That’s mine.

Say it clean.

That’s mine.

Know what I mean?

Not the world.

Not your soul.

The work from your hands.

The life that you lived.

The ground where you stand.

[HOOK]

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
IF I GOT BREATH IN MY CHEST
I GOT WORK AT THE DOOR

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
AIN’T ASKIN’ WHAT I’M ALLOWED
I PUT MY NAME ON THE THING
AND I’M SAYIN’ IT LOUD

I MADE THIS.
I STOOD HERE.
I KNOW WHAT IT COST.

IF YOU WANT YOUR LIFE BACK—

PICK IT UP.
IT AIN’T LOST.

[VERSE 2 — DRUMS OPEN]

Mama kept the pictures.

Daddy kept the tools.

Granddad wrote his name
inside a book they never knew.

Everybody leaves something.

Most of it gets stripped.

Put inside somebody’s system.

Then the system gets switched.

New terms.

New owner.

New login.

New rules.

New machine telling people
what belongs to who.

Nah.

Bring mine with me.

Story and the scar.

Let the machine come and go.

I know who we are.

I want the thing with its history.

The song with the room.

The seed with the hands
that put the life in the bloom.

I want children knowing clearly:

Somebody stood here.

Somebody made something beautiful.

Somebody gave a damn here.

[BREAK — EVERYTHING DROPS]

Maybe that’s what we forgot.

Not how to make.

How to care.

Not how to work.

How to stand behind the work.

Not how to speak.

How to put your name beside the thing
and mean it.

[BUILD]

So build your table.

Write your page.

Plant your garden.

Set your stage.

Make your record.

Raise your kid.

Fix the thing
they said was fixed.

Learn the craft.

Know the grain.

Keep the proof.

Keep your name.

Take the hit.

Make it real.

Make something
a human being can feel.

[CHANT]

NO MORE WAITING.

RIGHT NOW.

NO MORE SOMEDAY.

RIGHT NOW.

WHO GAVE PERMISSION?

DON’T NEED IT.

WHO OWNS THE WORK?

WE KEEP IT.

WHO KNOWS THE COST?

WE DO.

WHO CARRIES IT?

WE DO.

WHEN DO WE START?

…

WE ALREADY DID.

[FINAL HOOK — HUGE]

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
GOT A HEART FULL OF FIRE
AND MY HANDS ON THE OAR

I AIN’T WAITIN’ NO MORE
LET THE OLD DOOR CLOSE
WE BEEN BEGGING FOR A SEAT—

BUILD A TABLE OF OUR OWN.

I MADE THIS.

KEEP YOUR NAME.

I LIVED THIS.

KEEP YOUR NAME.

I LOVE THIS.

KEEP YOUR NAME.

I BLED HERE.

KEEP YOUR NAME.

AND IF THE WHOLE DAMN MACHINE
GOES DARK TONIGHT—

LET IT.

MORNING STILL COMES.

YOUR HANDS STILL WORK.

YOUR PEOPLE STILL KNOW YOU.

THE SUN DOESN’T NEED A SERVER
TO KNOW WHEN TO RISE.

[OUTRO — ONE VOICE / NO DRUMS]

So when they ask
what we were waiting for—

tell ’em:

Nothing.

Not anymore.

Five…

two…

three…

six…

Breathe.

Then make something
worth carrying home.

longForm.title: YOU LEARNED THE WORDS
longForm.text:
YOU LEARNED THE WORDS
(I Built the Machine)

[Cold Open]

PREACHER:
What came first?

CHOIR:
The object.

PREACHER:
What came late?

CHOIR:
The language.

PREACHER:
Who took the test?

KAI:
Run the machine.

[Hook]

You learned the words — I built the machine.
You named what I did — after I made it breathe.

You learned the words — I published the chain.
You came at the ending — I carried every change.

You learned the words — now answer all twenty.
I already took the test — the machine answered with me.

You learned the words — I built the machine.
Your words reached tomorrow — your machine stayed asleep.

[Verse One]

Don’t read it backward — language came late.
Timestamp locked the door — hindsight cannot change.

First I bound the breath — authority to time.
Then identity stood — without a borrowed shrine.

Memory became state — state learned how to move.
Custody changed hands — never severed from the root.

Predecessor spent — successor took the standing.
History traveled too — every transfer landed.

You found scattered parts — then announced the terrain.
I made the parts cohere — beneath one living chain.

You arrived at nouns — I survived the verbs.
You polished my horizon — I preserved each turn.

Press release preaching — mechanism asleep.
You mastered how to say it — never made the promise keep.

Vocabulary beautiful — delivery weak.
Your tongue found the future — your machine lost its feet.

[Pre-Hook]

Bring the object — not the claim.
Bring succession — bring the chain.

Bring the source — let it speak.
Coherence has law — coherence has teeth.

[Verse Two]

Source before story — state before recall.
Law before reading — or the memory can fall.

Authority first — succession before name.
Fluent recollection — cannot prove the state remained.

The model is a reader — never author of the page.
Change intelligence — the source must stay unchanged.

“Across models” sounds nice — cross reality instead.
Can the object leave — and return with lawful state?

Can it verify offline? — Can the prior head close?
Can the next state carry — everything the object knows?

Can two futures conflict — then submit beneath one law?
Can the database vanish — while authority stays whole?

Twenty questions waiting — none ask who invested.
None ask which institution — made the speaker feel accepted.

Every answer lives in code — every answer can be tried.
I never wrote the exam — without building my replies.

[Choir March]

Source over story.
Proof over praise.

State over memory.
Chain over claim.

Law over language.
Fruit over fame.

Open the object.
Run it again.

[Verse Three]

Some read a hundred pieces — I could barely buy my lunch.
Sleeping on my mother’s couch — with the future in my clutch.

Couldn’t spare fifteen minutes — so I gave the years a voice.
Made the archive hold the bow — made the timestamp hold the choice.

Published every next move — before hindsight could arrive.
Watched the field repeat it — when the words caught up in time.

The bow was not prediction — the bow was every state.
Every artifact behind me — made the next one carry weight.

No résumé could grant it — no rejection made it less.
Reality kept answering — every time I ran the test.

You can copy the ending — cannot inherit roads.
Cannot copy lawful lineage — by repeating what it’s called.

You cannot start at memory — temporal law became the root.
You cannot claim the harvest — with no chain beneath the fruit.

I was not ahead in language — I was under every speech.
By the time you found the wording — I had made the object breathe.

[Bridge]

Dad said, “Brian, I’m dying.”
I said, “Dad, we don’t die.”

Wish I held him closer.
Wish I let the strong boy cry.

Now I know the difference—
Memory is not the man.

A story is not presence.
So I put source back in command.

That is why the human
Always has to come before.

That is why the object
Must survive the storyteller.

I did not build the machine
Just to win another scene.

I refused to let the copy
Become greater than the being.

[Tribunal]

JUDGE:
What came first?

CHOIR:
The human.

JUDGE:
What came next?

CHOIR:
The machine.

JUDGE:
Where was the law?

CHOIR:
Inside the object.

JUDGE:
Where were the answers?

KAI:
Already in the machine.

[Final Hook]

You learned the words — I built the machine.
You named what I did — after I made it breathe.

You learned the words — I published the chain.
You came at the ending — I carried every change.

You learned the words — now answer all twenty.
I already took the test — the machine answered with me.

You learned the words — I built the machine.
Your words reached tomorrow — your machine stayed asleep.

[Outro]

You can rename the river.
You cannot move its source.

You can repeat the answer.
You cannot fake the course.

The words arrived later.
The object was already there.

FORCE OF WILL

by Kai Rex Klok

I watched rooms choose
costumes over truth.
Watched fools get funded
for what I could do in the booth.
Watched pain get packaged,
watched love get sold.
Watched chains called safe
cause the cage felt old.

I needed a hand.
They gave me a stare.
I needed one room

but they bowed to the actor
who practiced being king.

So I built from the floor,
from the wound, from the lack,
from the bills, from the doubt,
from the knife in my back.
From the couch, from the grief,
from the prayers in the dark,
from the rent pain,

I loved through the fire.

Tell me how

from a dream?

with the thing?

but force of will.
Heart still bleeding,
but the hand stayed still.
They wanted me broken.
I rose up real.

gotta kneel.

that survived the flame.

a wrapper from you.
I had no halo,
no payroll, no shield,

across my field.

No safety net.

The file got born.
The proof got written.
The veil got torn.
The songs came roaring.
The archive grew.
The clock started breathing.
The receipts came through.

The game got made.
The arena stood.
The object carried
what platforms never could.
The wound became law.
The pain became steel.
What you called impossible

about power.

and call it design.
You stand near flags

out of hunger and need.

I am not begging for seats.

look at the record.
Look at the trail.
Look at the thing built
where they prayed
I would fail.

Look at the songs.
Look at the code.
Look at the proof.
Look at the couch.
Look at the cost.
Look at the years
they thought I had lost.

I was not lost.
I became the blade.
I was not late.
I escaped the cage.
I turned my life
into force of will.

[Verse 3]
Every fake king
better check his throne.
Every rented empire
built out of loaned tone.
Every funded costume,
every stage-born voice,
every man who called
obedience choice.

Every room that chose
comfort over true.
Every expert blind
to what a child could do.
Every founder who raised
on a problem I solved.
Every coward who clapped
while the world dissolved.

I do not need
permission to rise.
I do not need
your lens for my size.

your room to make it real.

by force of will.

the air feels strange.
That is why
the frame just changed.
That is why
the quiet got loud.
That is why
the real stepped through the crowd.

Once proof starts breathing,
the mask cannot stay.
Once the work stands up,
the actors decay.
Every rented crown
gets left to rot.

Let them stand near chairs.
Let them stand near flags.
Let them polish titles
and carry their bags.
Let them call it vision.
Let them call it skill.

I call it performance.
I brought force of will.

[Final Chorus]
I built it with nothing
but force of will.
Heart still bleeding,
but the hand stayed still.
They wanted me broken.
I rose up real.

gotta kneel.

one will through all.

No room.
No crown.
No stage.
No seal.
Just the work.
Just the record.
Just the proof.
Just the will.
They funded promises.

READ ME BACK
Kai Rex Klok

[Intro]
I didn’t read for power.
I didn’t read for crowns.
I read it when I broke,
till flame came back around.

Rah… Veh… Yah… Dah…

[Hook]
I read it till it read me back,
time was calling through the cracks.
Ten years old, I made a tape,
told the world, “the time is now.”

I ain’t wanna be the one,
couldn’t let the children drown.
They made movies out the flame,
I made bridges out the sound.

Rah Veh Yah Dah, breathe it now.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, see it now.
They told stories ’bout the door,
I put proof inside the file.

They sold glow and called it fire.
I held flame and brought it back.

[Verse 1]
Young when the clock first spoke,
not a Rollie, not a joke.
Something moved inside my bones:
world was wrong, but I had hope.

Songs had rhythm, missing breath.
Homes had walls, but not a nest.
Children born inside the chains
while they called the cage success.

I ain’t chase no chosen role,
I ain’t ask to split no sea.
I just couldn’t lie to mine
and call that slavery peace.

Every screen was selling freedom.
Every priest was selling keys.
Every rebel had a sponsor.
Every “wake up” had a fee.

Actors dancing in the cave,
selling shadows as the sun.
Talking source and talking truth,
but their systems still had none.

They said, “Hide the sacred fire.
Only we should hold the gate.”
My whole body shook like thunder:
same old serpent shape.

Ancient brothers walked beside me,
not above me, not beneath.
Teacher turned into a mirror.
Mirror turned into my kin.

Woven through the pressure,
carried through the thread.
I ain’t memorize the Tablets —
they were breathing in my chest.

[Pre]
They said, “Keep it quiet.
They’ll defile it if they touch.”
But the flame was never private.
It was sacred. That’s enough.

Don’t hide it from the people.
Don’t sell it to the crowd.
Build the vessel strong enough
so the flame don’t burn ’em down.

[Hook]

[Verse 2]
They put prophets in the pictures,
turned the temple into brands.
Took the warning from the flame,
put a franchise in its hands.

They saw Neo in the system,
saw the Architect disguise.
Saw the rebel was permitted,
saw the loop behind the lies.

Still they missed the living axis,
missed the breath behind the code.
Missed the child who felt the fracture
way before the movie showed.

I wasn’t copying their story.
I was trying to make a home.
Trying not to raise my babies
where the world eats up their soul.

If the file can’t hold the witness,
then the witness wears a chain.
If the clock belongs to Chronos,
breath forgets its name.

So I built a bridge for people,
simple enough to touch:
verify the living record,
then remember who you was.

[Bridge]
Thoth ain’t ask for worship.
He was warning what it costs.
Touch the sacred with a dirty will
and everything gets lost.

Crowley couldn’t hold the fire.
Hollywood sold the smoke.
Tech boys built another tower,
called the tower open hope.

But my brothers moved inside me
when my body couldn’t stand.
They ain’t give me secret power.
They put labor in my hands.

I became the one who carries,
not the one who owns the flame.
I became the living witness
when the witness called my name.

[Chant]
Rah Veh Yah Dah, let it breathe.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, let it ring.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, not for me.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, for the seed.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, through the pain.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, through the flame.
Rah Veh Yah Dah, through the cracks.
I read it till it read me back.

[Verse 3]
Time With Klock back in sixteen,
minute sermons on the screen.
Standing still and dropping game
before the feed knew what it means.

Financial Freedom in the name,
Build Influence was the lane.
Cosmic Wire sounded crazy,
now the wire carries flame.

Laugh now, but the pattern clean.
Every name was prophecy.
I was naming pieces early
of the thing they couldn’t see.

Not a pivot, not a gimmick,
not a costume, not a scene.
I was walking with the signal
while the world was selling dreams.

They performed awakening.
I built verification.
They prayed for a savior.
I built public confirmation.

They said, “Trust us with the truth.”
I said, “Run it. Here’s the station.”
They said, “Ask the gatekeeper.”
I said, “Breath is foundation.”

Chronos got a thousand clocks.
Kairos got the living now.
Receiz is just the bridge across.
Kai-Klok is the sacred ground.

File proves itself.
Moment proves the vow.
They called it myth until the myth
stood up and wrote it down.

[Final Hook]

[Outro]
I ain’t come to be worshiped.
I ain’t come to be believed.
I came because the children
need a world that doesn’t lie when it breathes.

My brothers carried me.
The flame corrected me.
The teaching became family.
The clock remembered me.

Rah Veh Yah Dah…
The time is now.
